sections.heading: Radians, degrees, and the unit circle

questions.q: Convert $150^\circ$ to radians, and convert $\dfrac{5\pi}{4}$ radians to degrees.
Find the exact coordinates of the point on the unit circle at angle $\theta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$.
questions.answer: $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}=120^\circ$, a reference angle of $60^\circ$ in Quadrant II. Coordinates: $\left(-\dfrac{1}{2},\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.

sections.heading: Exact values from the unit circle

questions.q: Find the exact values of $\sin\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right)$.
The graph shows $f(x)=\sin(x)$ and $g(x)=\cos(x)$ over one period.
parts: State the amplitude and period of each function shown.
Identify the horizontal shift that maps $\sin(x)$ onto $\cos(x)$.
answers: Both curves have amplitude $1$ and period $2\pi$, matching the single full up-down cycle shown across the interval.
$\cos(x)=\sin\left(x+\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, so shifting $\sin(x)$ left by $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ produces $\cos(x)$ — visible as the cosine curve reaching its peak a quarter-period earlier.

questions.q: State the amplitude, period, and vertical shift of $f(x)=3\sin(2x)+1$.
A Ferris wheel's height above the ground is modeled by $h(t)=20\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}t\right)+22$, where $t$ is in minutes. Find the maximum height, minimum height, and period of one full rotation.
questions.answer: Maximum height $=22+20=42$ m. Minimum height $=22-20=2$ m. Period $=\dfrac{2\pi}{\pi/6}=12$ minutes.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=\dfrac{3}{5}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant II, find $\cos\theta$ and $\tan\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\dfrac{9}{25}=\dfrac{16}{25}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{4}{5}$. In Quadrant II, cosine is negative: $\cos\theta=-\dfrac{4}{5}$. $\tan\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}=\dfrac{3/5}{-4/5}=-\dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.q: Find $\sec\theta$ and $\csc\theta$ if $\cos\theta=-\dfrac{5}{13}$ and $\theta$ is in Quadrant III.

The average daily temperature in a city is modeled by $T(m)=15\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}(m-3)\right)+18$ degrees Celsius, where $m$ is the month number ($m=1$ for January). Find the temperature in April ($m=4$) and state the month of maximum temperature.
questions.answer: $T(4)=15\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}(1)\right)+18=15\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)+18=15(0.5)+18=25.5^\circ$C. Maximum occurs when $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}(m-3)\right)=1$, i.e. $\dfrac{\pi}{6}(m-3)=\dfrac{\pi}{2}$, giving $m-3=3$, so $m=6$ (June).

questions.q: A wheel of radius 10 cm rotates at 4 revolutions per second. Find its angular speed $\omega$ in radians per second, and the linear speed of a point on its rim.
questions.answer: $\omega=4\times2\pi=8\pi$ rad/s (4 revolutions per second, each revolution $=2\pi$ radians). Linear speed $v=r\omega=10(8\pi)=80\pi\approx251.3$ cm/s.

questions.q: A satellite orbits Earth at a radius of 7000 km, completing one orbit every 2 hours. Find its linear speed in km/h.
questions.answer: Angular speed $\omega=\dfrac{2\pi}{2}=\pi$ rad/h. Linear speed $v=r\omega=7000\pi\approx21{,}991$ km/h.

Given $\sin\theta=\frac{20}{29}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant I, find $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\left(\frac{20}{29}\right)^2=\dfrac{441}{841}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{21}{29}$. In Quadrant I, cosine is positive: $\cos\theta=\frac{21}{29}$.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=\frac{5}{13}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant I, find $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\left(\frac{5}{13}\right)^2=\dfrac{144}{169}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{12}{13}$. In Quadrant I, cosine is positive: $\cos\theta=\frac{12}{13}$.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=-\frac{20}{29}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant IV, find $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\left(-\frac{20}{29}\right)^2=\dfrac{441}{841}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{21}{29}$. In Quadrant IV, cosine is positive: $\cos\theta=\frac{21}{29}$.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant I, find $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\left(\frac{8}{17}\right)^2=\dfrac{225}{289}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{15}{17}$. In Quadrant I, cosine is positive: $\cos\theta=\frac{15}{17}$.

questions.q: Given $\sin\theta=\frac{3}{5}$ with $\theta$ in Quadrant I, find $\cos\theta$.
questions.answer: Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$: $\cos^2\theta=1-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2=\dfrac{16}{25}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\dfrac{4}{5}$. In Quadrant I, cosine is positive: $\cos\theta=\frac{4}{5}$.
